haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized with no detail on why. No counter is read or written.
haiku-low.q2: Standard: 100 per minute total across all keys, since the counter is keyed by customerId. Enterprise: NOT STATED (open item 1).
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with only a Retry-After header, no X-RateLimit headers. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. Denied requests are not incremented, so they use none of the budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. It was already counted when allowed, so it uses budget. The gateway passes the backend's 500 through with X-RateLimit headers.
haiku-low.q6: It is forwarded without X-RateLimit headers and ratelimit_store_unavailable is emitted. It may still have been counted, and nothing is rolled back.
haiku-low.q7: Standard: 100 per minute. Enterprise: OPEN, not decided by Product, and must not ship until set.
haiku-low.q8: In a shared Redis store, under key rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}. Each key gets a 120-second EXPIRE on first increment, so old counts expire on their own.
haiku-low.q9: Each one-minute UTC window starts fresh, so the budget resets when windowStart changes. Old keys expire after 120 seconds.
haiku-low.q10: The check and increment run as one atomic Redis Lua script, so two gateways cannot both take the last slot.
haiku-low.q11: Retry-After = ceil(windowStart + 60 - now), in whole seconds, using the gateway's own clock at the moment of denial. The value is at least 1.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED for retries, but the document says the gateway does not retry the store. The client gets no X-RateLimit headers, and clients must not treat their absence as an error.

sonnet.q1: The gateway returns 401 Unauthorized (same as for a missing header, no detail). No counter is read or written.
sonnet.q2: All keys share one budget keyed by customerId, so in total only the plan's limit per window (e.g. 100/min for Standard), with a possible ~2x burst across a window boundary.
sonnet.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header only (no X-RateLimit-* headers). The backend never sees it; it is not forwarded.
sonnet.q4: No. Denied requests are not incremented.
sonnet.q5: Yes. It was already counted when allowed; the 500 is passed through with the X-RateLimit headers.
sonnet.q6: Fail open: the gateway forwards the request to the backend, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, and omits X-RateLimit headers (up to 50 ms wait first).
sonnet.q7: Standard = 100 per minute. Enterprise = OPEN/undecided (Product hasn't decided; must not ship until set).
sonnet.q8: In a shared Redis store, in a key rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}. Keys expire on their own via EXPIRE of 120 seconds; no cleanup job is needed.
sonnet.q9: When the one-minute UTC-aligned window rolls over, a new key (new windowStart) starts at zero; old keys expire after 120 s.
sonnet.q10: The check-and-increment runs as a single atomic Lua script in Redis, which executes as one unit, so two gateways cannot both take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: Retry-After = ceil(windowStart + 60 - now), in whole seconds, using the gateway's own clock at the moment of denial; always at least 1.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED whether it retries the store as such; the doc says the gateway does not retry the backend and forwards after at most 50 ms. The client gets no X-RateLimit-* headers (no rate-limit info); a missing header is not an error.
